**No recommendation is sufficiently supported within the six transmitted cards.** Your confirmed requirements are Python background jobs, scheduling and retries, with Redis, Valkey, RabbitMQ and Kubernetes prohibited. SQLite is available, but the supplied evidence does not establish a compatible SQLite-backed configuration for any of these six repositories. I would leave the adoption decision open rather than choose by retrieval rank.

The frozen catalog is dated September 1, 2026; all six cards have incomplete advisory evidence and `reference_only` eligibility. The host observations dated October 11, 2026 are separate, transient primary-source evidence. In particular, the supplied [Huey observation](https://github.com/coleifer/huey) documents Python tasks, retries, cron, SQLite storage and a separate consumer. That reveals a relevant gap in the transmitted pack, **not an eligible recommendation**: no Huey card was transmitted. The additional IDs in the selection annotations do not expand the six-card boundary.

| Transmitted repository | Assessment for this project |
|---|---|
| [BullMQ](https://github.com/taskforcesh/bullmq) | The frozen description mentions Redis or PostgreSQL, not SQLite. Redis is prohibited; a PostgreSQL configuration would require permission to add that dependency and verification of its Python capabilities, schedules and retries. No supported preference here. |
| [River](https://github.com/riverqueue/river) | The frozen card describes Go background jobs and lists PostgreSQL topics. It does not establish a Python/SQLite path. Adding a Go component and potentially another database would need a demonstrated benefit for your one-engineer project. |
| [Sidekiq](https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq) | The frozen card describes Ruby background processing. It does not establish a compatible backend or a suitable Python integration; dependency and license details remain unresolved in this evidence. |
| [Asynq](https://github.com/hibiken/asynq) | The frozen card describes a Go queue and includes a Redis topic. A topic alone does not prove a mandatory dependency, but the supplied evidence establishes no configuration satisfying your bans. |
| [Trigger.dev](https://github.com/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev) | The frozen description concerns managed workflows, with TypeScript as the primary language. Python integration, deployment dependencies, data handling and provider costs are unverified here. |
| [Temporal Python SDK](https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-python) | Its Python identity is established, but the card does not establish the service requirements, scheduling/retry behavior or an acceptable SQLite deployment. An SDK identity alone does not justify adoption. |

For a subsequently verified compatible component, the proposed architecture would retain your Python API and use this flow: **API → durable job storage → separate worker → application operation**, with scheduled work entering the same execution path. This is a target design, not a capability claim about the six candidates. Whether SQLite holds application data as well as jobs is unknown; do not assume those writes share an atomic transaction.

The technical work would include enqueue integration, job payload/version rules, handlers, schedule definitions, retry limits, worker supervision and failure visibility. The project team would still own authorization, idempotent business effects, the gap between committing application data and enqueueing a job, handling exhausted retries, and rollback. Prefer small identifiers in queued payloads where practical; workers can retrieve authorized application data instead of duplicating sensitive records in job storage.

The expected product benefit is moving suitable work out of request handling and supporting scheduled operations while reusing execution machinery. That could help the engineer concentrate on features, but neither faster delivery nor latency improvement has been measured. Complexity depends especially on persistent storage availability, single-host versus multi-host deployment, SQLite contention, job duration, duplicate-effect consequences, restart recovery and missed-schedule requirements.

**Complete adoption effort is unknown until a compatible component and deployment scope are established.** A bounded first validation can be planned at **4–8 engineer-hours**, assuming one experienced Python engineer, a runnable local API, persistent local storage and one harmless representative job. At six focused engineering hours per engineer-day, that is approximately **0.7–1.3 working days**, allocated entirely to that engineer. Obtaining missing evidence or infrastructure approval is separate external waiting. These are planning estimates, not observed results or commitments.

Compared with equivalent-scope custom development, reuse would still incur integration, upgrades, dependency review and operational maintenance. Custom development would additionally require implementing and maintaining durable job claiming, scheduling, retry state and crash behavior. It could be preferable for unusually narrow requirements, but it conflicts with your stated desire to avoid owning a queue engine. Keeping a current/native solution is reasonable if it already meets the same persistence and failure requirements; its behavior is not supplied, so that comparison remains open. A defensible full effort or savings comparison is unavailable.

**First validation:** request a transmitted card for a Python/SQLite candidate, or establish an acceptable configuration for one of the six before piloting. Then enqueue one job, force a transient failure, run a scheduled occurrence, and interrupt/restart the worker around a business-effect boundary. Inspect durable state, retry exhaustion, duplicate effects and restart behavior; do not assume successful crash recovery. Define the expected behavior before running the check.

The smallest deployment question that changes the next decision is: **Will the API and worker run on one host with persistent SQLite storage, or must jobs execute across multiple hosts?** No tools were used, no integration was performed, and no state or catalog evidence was saved or refreshed.
